title: IEEE-754 negative zero survives; the JSON integer -0 does not
measurementNote: CORRECTION. The designer marked this JSON-only on the grounds that the MAP stack cannot observe the integer arm. Measurement shows the JSON stack cannot observe EITHER arm, so as declared the fixture was vacuous: the integer sign is gone at Jackson parse time so it is absent from the baseline as well as the result, and the double sign is invisible under exact-decimal comparison because BigDecimal has no signed zero (both -0.0 and 0.0 render as 0.0). Widened to BOTH. The MAP arm is now the live one: it renders Double.toString, so -0.0 and 0.0 stay distinct and the fixture goes red the moment reconstruction normalises the sign away. Measured LOSSLESS, not ACCEPTED_LOSS: the integer -0 is lost before flatten() is ever called, which is a property of JSON parsing and not of the round trip under test.
rationale: The contract test celebrates that negative zero is preserved, but only for -0.0d at the Map level. JSON permits -0 as an INTEGER too, and that arm behaves differently: Jackson reads an int token and the sign is gone before the flattener runs. Both in one document makes the boundary explicit instead of implied.
catchesBugClass: A reconstruction path that normalises -0.0 to 0.0, and any oracle using == or equals on boxed Doubles rather than Double.compare.
cannotCatch: Marked JSON-only because the MAP stack cannot observe the integer arm. It also does not exercise -0.0 inside an array, nor under the delimiter formats.

predicted.detail: negDouble keeps its sign bit; negInt loses its minus sign. Defensible: no Java integral type can represent a signed zero and preserving it would require promoting every -0 to a double.
